claims.text: The starting material is a W–Cu composite with discrete W particles or interconnected W ligaments embedded in a Cu matrix.
Untreated W–Cu composites are prone to phase separation and interfacial void formation under high-temperature and irradiation exposure.
A W–Ta–Cr–V composition is a suitable example of a refractory HEA for the proposed interlayer.
Sputtering or chemical vapor deposition can place a thin, conformal HEA layer at the internal W/Cu interfaces before final consolidation.
The proposed exposure envelope extends to approximately 1500 °C and includes Ar+, He+, and D+ irradiation.
These thermal and ion-exposure conditions are representative of W-based plasma-facing material joints with Cu-based cooling components.
The deposited layer will form a stable, nanostructured HEA interphase.
The HEA interphase will act as a graded transition between refractory W and ductile Cu.
The HEA interlayer will reduce interfacial-energy mismatch at W/Cu interfaces.
The HEA interlayer will promote chemical and structural compatibility between W and Cu.
Improved interfacial compatibility will inhibit void nucleation and minimize phase separation.
Suppressing interfacial damage will preserve continuous, low-resistance heat-transfer pathways during cyclic thermal and irradiation stresses.
HEA-interlayer composites will retain a more uniform and continuous interface with fewer voids and less phase separation than untreated controls.
HEA-interlayer composites will have higher thermal conductivity than untreated W–Cu composites after equivalent thermal and irradiation exposure.
The benefit depends on the HEA interlayer remaining continuous and stable during prolonged thermal cycling and irradiation.
The benefit may diminish if the interlayer reacts adversely or destabilizes above an unspecified irradiation-dose threshold.
Related W/Ta-containing refractory multicomponent alloys can retain their constituent phase structures after eight days at 1500 °C.
Prior evidence shows that multi-element interlayers modify interfacial energies.
The optimal HEA composition, interlayer thickness, and long-term behavior under combined heat and particle irradiation remain undetermined.
Failure to obtain a statistically significant reduction in interfacial damage or any thermal-conductivity improvement relative to an untreated control would falsify the hypothesis.
